subject: general
question: The Supreme Court struck down certain provisions of the Tribunals (Rationalisation and Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 2021. Which provision did the Court declare invalid?

options.text: The rule that tribunal decisions are not appealable to any court
Requirement that all tribunal members be retired judges of High Courts
Establishment of administrative tribunals for service matters (which is in the Constitution)
A fixed four-year tenure limit for tribunal members

solution:
The correct answer is __**A fixed four-year tenure limit for tribunal members**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Supreme Court of India** struck down provisions of the **Tribunals (Rationalisation and Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 2021** that imposed a fixed **four-year tenure limit** for tribunal members.
 
• This decision was based on the principle that tribunal members must have sufficient tenure to ensure **independence** and a fair decision-making process. The fixed tenure of four years was seen as insufficient to maintain the integrity of the tribunal system.
 
• The Court emphasized that the independence of tribunals is a key element of the judicial process and reducing the tenure to four years undermines this independence. *Hence, this provision was declared invalid.*
